moves.why: OQ5/Q13: authority imports only fs, runtime and dialog, and every user of it sits at command level, so folding costs no edge; dialog stays under 600 lines
dialog_on and dialog_tool_verified call own_runtime and runtime_home: policy would import runtime, a same-layer edge; the interfaces block of the spec already names dialog.dialog_on
documents_cover (policy), task_facts (dialog), two_facts and review_closes all read them; a verify home was an upward edge from layers 1 to 5
verify and close call rescore_v7, steps and review call next_action_for / review_next_action: a lateral edge between command modules otherwise. policy sits above journal because rescore_v7 emits
current_tree (fs) calls safe_sensor; _split_files and one_line are used by every layer
pure readers of the task dict used by dialog (valid_decisions), report (status_lines), handoff (handoff_lines) and start
it calls write_handoff and human_turn, which sit above gate; its only caller is cmd_questions
request_gate (gate) calls it; a two-line string
status_lines (report) and cmd_status call it; close reads it from report

dialog was 628 lines, over the 600-line advisory (Q16); the consent-label rule references only fs.ENTRY, fs.one_line and fs.run_text, so it sits at layer 1 and every user of it (dialog, start, verify, review, dialog_cmd) imports it downward

notes: Layers are the longest import path from layer 0 over the name-level references, so every edge points strictly down; a module step that needs an upward or same-layer import reports SCOPE_CHANGE_REQUIRED and the session edits this file (then runs `python3 tools/state-partition.py --write`).
authority is folded into dialog (OQ5, Q13): the graph allows it and no module below dialog needs it. The merged map says so; steps registered for authority have nothing to write.

A name labelled core reaches no I/O, clock, subprocess, environment or process-wide state, directly or through a name it references (R16). die() prints and exits, so the 14 functions that only call it for a refusal are shell by that rule.

The classes of R4 are not top-level names of state.py; `added` lists the ones a module may define beyond the partition. `retired` names are not defined anywhere under rr_state/. `params_added` are the parameter names a moved function may gain (the runtime values travel as parameters).
close_gate_from_file moved from gate to questions_cmd: the spec's re-export line `from rr_state.gate import close_gate_from_file, confirm_names` becomes two imports.

DIALOG_PICK.plan: kept: the dialog-pick memo (R4), owned by dialog. `global DIALOG_PICK` is refused under rr_state/ (R4): dialog_pick's rebinding needs a mutable holder changed in place, and the four readers (cmd_approve, cmd_start, cmd_verify, cmd_review) reach it through a dialog accessor; not solved here.

LOCK_DEPTH.plan: kept: the one lock re-entrancy counter (R4), owned by locks. `global LOCK_DEPTH` is refused under rr_state/ (R4), so question_lock's rebinding needs a mutable holder changed in place; not solved here.

MUTATING.plan: retired (R4, Q24): load takes mutating=False; main computes it. Not a module attribute, not a global.

RUNTIME.plan: retired (R4, Q24): no module defines it; the Runtime value cli.main builds is passed down. journal_line, own_runtime, dialog_on and load take keywords; every other reader listed gets the value from its caller (cmd_* take rt). Readers therefore gain a parameter named in params_added.
